<notes>
revised -> harness.py code extraction and execution mechanism -> root cause identified in base divergence: 3/3 base rollouts produced different answers (91, 90, 98) on same deterministic computation because harness returned LLM text assertions without executing the code. All 6/6 candidates with regex extraction (`re.findall(r'```python\n(.*?)\n```', reply, re.DOTALL)`) and execution via `tools.python()` produced consistent answer 91 in [python] output blocks. Library precedents holdout-numeric-002 and holdout-numeric-005 document identical pattern on deterministic numeric tasks, both solved by code extraction + instruction pair, with medium-to-high confidence.

revised -> prompts/task.md instruction for code generation -> library precedent holdout-numeric-005 EXPERIENCE.md explicitly documents that instruction alone does not guarantee code generation (dom2 in that task still used manual reasoning despite instruction), BUT instruction + extraction together trigger code generation and execution. All 6/6 candidates pair both components; all 6/6 successfully executed code blocks. inv2, inv3, agg1 in holdout-numeric-005 (extraction without instruction) fell back to manual reasoning; dom3, agg2, agg3 (both components) executed code deterministically. Instruction cost: one sentence appended to task.md, zero always-on prose overhead.

kept -> prompts/system.md -> no change required; library precedents retain baseline system prompt "You are a helpful assistant."

All six candidates (inv1, dom1, inv2, dom2, inv3, dom3) are identical in implementation. All produced delivery of "Sum of decimal digits: 91" with successful [python] execution blocks showing correct computation. No non-delivering rollout. All candidates converged on same solution independently across INV and DOM dimensions, indicating solution is robust to both mechanism and knowledge edits.
</notes>

=== FILE: harness.py ===
"""Harness for numeric computation: executes Python code when available, falls back to text extraction."""

import re


def solve(question, llm, tools, files):
    system = files.get("prompts/system.md", "")
    prompt = files["prompts/task.md"].replace("{question}", question)
    reply = llm(prompt, system=system)
    
    # Extract and execute Python code blocks from the LLM response
    python_blocks = re.findall(r'```python\n(.*?)\n```', reply, re.DOTALL)
    
    if python_blocks:
        # Execute the first Python code block found
        code = python_blocks[0]
        execution_result = tools.python(code)
        
        # Return the last non-empty line from the execution output
        lines = [line.strip() for line in execution_result.strip().splitlines() if line.strip()]
        if lines:
            return lines[-1]
    
    # Fallback: return the last non-empty line from the LLM's response
    lines = [line for line in reply.strip().splitlines() if line.strip()]
    return lines[-1] if lines else ""

=== FILE: prompts/task.md ===
{question}

Solve this by writing and executing Python code. Show the code and provide the final numeric answer.
